ukmt-sk-2025-01.title: Group the factors
ukmt-sk-2025-01.body:
$7\times11\times13=1001$ and $2\times3\times5=30$, so the product is $30030$. The remainder on division by $100$ is $r=30$, so $200-r=170$.

**Answer: 170**

ukmt-sk-2025-02.title: Match the sectors
ukmt-sk-2025-02.body:
The sectors $12\%$ and $11\%$ are about equal, so they are car and walk. Among the others, $47\%$ and $24\%$ are roughly in ratio $2:1$, so they are bicycle and bus. The train is the remaining sector, $6\%$ of $2000=120$.

**Answer: 120**

ukmt-sk-2025-03.title: Add by place value
ukmt-sk-2025-03.body:
Each letter appears once in each of the hundreds, tens and units places, so the sum is $111(A+B+C+D+E)=2664$. Hence $A+B+C+D+E=24$ and $10\times24=240$.

**Answer: 240**

ukmt-sk-2025-04.title: Residues mod 7
ukmt-sk-2025-04.body:
Work modulo $7$. $n=100\equiv2$: the factors are $11\equiv4$, $11\equiv4$, $6$: none is $0$. $n=101\equiv3$: $16\equiv2$, $17\equiv3$, $25\equiv4$: none is $0$. $n=102\equiv4$: $5\cdot4+1=21\equiv0$, so the product is divisible by $7$. The answer is $102$.

**Answer: 102**

ukmt-sk-2025-05.title: Bound b
ukmt-sk-2025-05.body:
$a=1$, $b=c=2^8=256$ works. If $b>2^8$ then $c\ge b>2^8$ as well, so $abc>2^{16}$ (with $a\ge1$). So the largest $b$ is $256$.

**Answer: 256**

ukmt-sk-2025-06.title: Add the three cases
ukmt-sk-2025-06.body:
All red: $\frac36\cdot\frac26\cdot\frac16=\frac6{216}$. All white: $\frac26\cdot\frac26\cdot\frac26=\frac8{216}$. All blue: $\frac16\cdot\frac26\cdot\frac36=\frac6{216}$. Total $\frac{20}{216}=\frac{100}{1080}$, so $K=100$.

**Answer: 100**

ukmt-sk-2025-07.title: Difference of squares
ukmt-sk-2025-07.body:
$(2025+t)^2-(2025-t)^2=4\cdot2025\,t$. So the numerator is $4\cdot2025\,(20+25)=4\cdot2025\cdot45=364500$. Dividing by $1000$ gives $364.5$, which rounds up to $365$.

**Answer: 365**

ukmt-sk-2025-09.title: Shift the window
ukmt-sk-2025-09.body:
Label the numbers $c_1,\dots,c_{19}$ around the circle. Comparing the sums of nine consecutive terms starting at $c_i$ and $c_{i+1}$ gives $c_i=c_{i+9}$ (indices mod $19$). Since $9$ and $19$ are coprime, repeatedly adding $9$ visits every position, so all nineteen numbers are equal. Then $9c=2025$, so each is $225$, and so is the largest.

**Answer: 225**

ukmt-sk-2025-10.title: Similar triangles
ukmt-sk-2025-10.body:
The smallest square has side $3$, the middle one side $9$. The side of the largest square passes through the top-left corner of the middle square and the top-left corner of the smallest square; the small right triangle has legs $3$ and $6$, hypotenuse $\sqrt{45}$. The larger right triangle (below, with height $9$) is similar with ratio $3$, so its hypotenuse is $3\sqrt{45}$. The side of the largest square is $\sqrt{45}+3\sqrt{45}=4\sqrt{45}$, with area $16\cdot45=720$.

**Answer: 720**

ukmt-sk-2025-11.title: Parity pattern
ukmt-sk-2025-11.body:
Parities: $k_1,k_2$ odd, $k_3=30$ even, then odd + even = odd, even + odd = odd, odd + odd = even, ... The pattern odd, odd, even repeats with period $3$. Since $2025=3\times675$, exactly $675$ terms are even.

**Answer: 675**

ukmt-sk-2025-12.title: Pythagoras
ukmt-sk-2025-12.body:
The circle is tangent to $AB$ and $AD$ at distance $15$ from $A$, so its radius is $15$ and the centre $O$ is $15$ from each of those sides. $AB=15+12=27$. Let $P$ be on $BC$ with $OP\perp BC$; then $OP=MB=12$ and $OC=15$, so $PC=\sqrt{225-144}=9$. Thus $BC=BP+PC=15+9=24$ and the area is $27\times24=648$.

**Answer: 648**

ukmt-sk-2025-13.title: Read the graph
ukmt-sk-2025-13.body:
The parabola opens upward, so $a>0$. It meets the $y$-axis below the origin, so $c<0$. Its lowest point is at positive $x$, i.e. $-\frac b{2a}>0$, so $b<0$. Then $ab<0$, $bc>0$, $ca<0$, $b+c<0$, $abc>0$. The positive ones are $a$, $bc$ and $abc$: $3$.

**Answer: 3**

ukmt-sk-2025-14.title: Area comparison
ukmt-sk-2025-14.body:
Let the original sides be $x$ and $y$; the new square has area $1.2x\cdot1.5y=1.8xy$. The shaded region lies between the square's diagonal and the original rectangle's diagonal, which share a corner; the area on one side of the square's diagonal is $0.5\cdot1.8xy$ and the part of the original rectangle on that side is $0.5xy$. So the shaded area is $0.9xy-0.5xy=0.4xy=210$, giving $xy=525$.

**Answer: 525**

ukmt-sk-2025-15.title: Dependent equations
ukmt-sk-2025-15.body:
Two linear equations in $x,y$ have more than one solution only if one is a multiple of the other (the same line). The left side of (2) is $2\times$ that of (1), so $a+b=2(a-b)$, i.e. $a=3b$. The left side of (4) is $3\times$ that of (3), so $a+4b-1=3(a-b+4)$, i.e. $2a=7b-13$. With $a=3b$: $6b=7b-13$, so $b=13$, $a=39$ and $10a+b=403$.

**Answer: 403**

ukmt-sk-2025-16.title: Angle sum
ukmt-sk-2025-16.body:
The angles sum to $720^\circ$: $6a+15d=720$. Since $a$ and $a+d$ are multiples of $10$, so is $d$, and $d\ne0$ (non-regular). $d=10$ gives $a=95$; $d=30$ gives $a=45$: neither is a multiple of $10$. $d=20$ gives $a=70$ and the angles $70,\dots,170$ are all below $180$. For $d\ge40$, $a+5d\ge200$ (since $a>0$) is not convex. So $a=70$, $d=20$ and $7a+11d=490+220=710$.

**Answer: 710**

ukmt-sk-2025-18.title: Binomial counts
ukmt-sk-2025-18.body:
Let class A have $P$ students. Then $\frac{P(P-1)}2=3\cdot\frac{(P-4)(P-5)}2$, so $P^2-P=3P^2-27P+60$, i.e. $2P^2-26P+60=0$, $P^2-13P+30=0$, $(P-10)(P-3)=0$. $P=3$ would make class B negative, so $P=10$.

**Answer: 10**

ukmt-sk-2025-19.title: Which element fails
ukmt-sk-2025-19.body:
Such a number fails to be divisible by exactly one element $m$ of $\{2,\dots,9\}$. Failing $2$, $3$ or $4$ forces failing $4,6,8$ / $6,9$ / $8$ as well, and failing only $6$ is impossible (divisibility by $2$ and $3$ gives $6$). The remaining cases: $m=8$ needs a multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(1..7,9)=1260$, too big; $m=5$: multiples of $504$ below $1000$: only $504$; $m=7$: multiples of $360$: $360,720$; $m=9$: multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}(1..8)=840$ not of $2520$: $840$. The largest is $840$.

**Answer: 840**

ukmt-sk-2025-20.title: Fill the grid
ukmt-sk-2025-20.body:
$1221=3\cdot11\cdot37$, so its two-digit factors are $11,33,37$. 1 ACROSS and 1 DOWN are different and share their tens digit, so they are $33$ and $37$ in some order.

**If 1 ACROSS $=33$:** 1 DOWN $=37$ and 2 DOWN $=343$ (the only three-digit cube starting with $3$). 3 ACROSS has the form $7\,4\,\_$ and is a multiple of $17$: $748=17\cdot44$. Then 4 DOWN is $8\_$, a prime: $83$ or $89$, and 5 ACROSS is $33$ or $39$, neither prime. Contradiction.

**So 1 ACROSS $=37$:** 1 DOWN $=33$ and 2 DOWN $=729$ (the only cube starting with $7$). 3 ACROSS has the form $3\,2\,\_$ and is a multiple of $17$: $323=17\cdot19$. 4 DOWN is $3\_$, a prime: $31$ or $37$, giving 5 ACROSS $=91=7\cdot13$ or $97$; only $97$ is prime.

The sum is $37+323+97=457$.

**Answer: 457**
